description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs:448
Issue: After every successful create_object for a Direct chat, handle_chat_set unconditionally calls get_objects::<Chat> again (line 448) to check for concurrent duplicates. In the no-race case — which is essentially 100% of production traffic — this is a full-collection fetch that serves no purpose: there will never be more than one copy, and the newly created object is already known. This means N Direct-chat creates in a single Chat/set request cost N+1 full-collection fetches (1 hoisted + N post-create), not 1.
Impact: Every successful Direct chat creation pays an extra full backend read. In bulk-create scenarios (e.g. contact sync) this N+1 pattern compounds. For backends where get_objects is a database scan, this is measurable latency.
Fix: Only perform the post-create re-fetch when there is actual evidence of concurrency (e.g., the backend returns a conflict/duplicate error), or gate it behind a runtime flag. Alternatively, replace the optimistic create-then-validate with a backend-level upsert or conditional-create primitive that returns alreadyExists atomically.
title: chat/set: post-create re-fetch on every Direct create (no-race common case)
